6126.strength_name: tracks on the smaller side of the change
6126.summary: Between 2018 Q4 and 2022 Q4 the recipe on Laser 2 (DLTS) changed. Units leaving the laser inside their trim limits went from 87% (327 tracks) to 98% (1,027 tracks), a move of +11 points. Median incoming resistance was 3,256 before and 2,840 after, so the recipe is not the only thing that changed. More than one limit table was in use (2 before, 1 after). A pass rate is a verdict against a test, so part of this move may be a change in which test was applied, not in the parts. On the 281-point table alone the move was 84% (251 tracks, 2018-05-09 to 2018-10-30) to 98% (1,027 tracks, 2022-10-06 to 2025-02-24).
6126.title: Laser 2 (DLTS): recipe changed from 1 cut (cut length 0.95) to 1 cut (cut length 0.85)

6126.strength_name: percentage points, best laser vs worst
6126.summary: On the same 281-point limit table, over the 14 months both ran it (2023-07 to 2025-02), Laser 2 (DLTS) passed 99% of 488 tracks against Laser 1 (LTS)'s 76% of 610. Settings that work on one laser may not transfer; this compares what each laser achieved on the same test in the same months, not why.
6126.title: Laser 2 (DLTS) passes 99%, Laser 1 (LTS) 76%, same test and months

6126.strength_name: share of that year graded against the second-busiest table
6126.summary: In the 12 months to 2026-09-14 Laser 1 (LTS) graded Track A against 2 different limit tables at the same time (the two busiest overlap by 115 days). The earlier one: 141 graded points (141 rows), 617 tracks, the central 90% of them between 2025-11-12 and 2026-08-24, 89% left the laser inside limits. The later one: 57 graded points (57 rows), 166 tracks, the central 90% of them between 2026-04-30 and 2026-09-11, 88% left the laser inside limits. Both carry the same band wherever their travel overlaps (56 positions compared), but one grades 141 points and the other 57. Linearity is zero-tolerance per point, so the denser table is the stricter test of the two. Pass rates measured against different tables are not comparable.
6126.title: Laser 1 (LTS): 2 limit tables were in service at once

6607.gain_definition: percentage points of tracks leaving the laser inside their per-point linearity limits, best setting versus the setting now running, on one machine and one limit table
6607.strength_name: points more often inside limits
6607.summary: On the same limit table, 6800 left 87% of 813 tracks inside their linearity limits against 60% of 1,283 at 6900 (a lower setting). It wins in both halves of incoming resistance (84% vs 54% below 4255.5 ohm, 90% vs 67% above), so the ink does not explain it. The laser moved from 6800 to 6900 in 2024-10 and has been 27 points worse since. That makes this a comparison of two PERIODS, so a change in material or handling over the same months cannot be ruled out from the data alone. It is cheap to settle: alternate 6800 and 6900 by lot for a week and this page will read the answer back. Worth asking why the setting changed in 2024-10.
6607.title: Laser 1 (LTS): cut 6800 passed 27 points more often than the 6900 now running

evidence.comparison: one-sided rank test (Mann-Whitney U, normal approximation with tie correction): the final-test / laser worst-error ratios of the 244 reworked unit-days against those of the 139 pass/pass unit-days in the top third of laser error (0.0332 V and up), over the travel both stations grade; confirmed at p < 0.01 with the rework median at 0.9x theirs or less

facts.reduction: per track the latest final test against that track's last laser attempt; per unit-day the track with the largest laser error

6607.strength_name: reworked units' median final-test/laser error ratio, as a share of the untouched units' that started nearest them
6607.summary: 261 unit-days in the last year failed linearity at the laser and then passed final test. That is hand trim, not an unnecessary rejection: their error fell more between the stations than it did for the untouched units that started nearest them. Over the travel both stations grade, each corrected with its own offset, final test's worst error on 244 of these units is a median 81% of the laser's on the same track, against 100% on the 139 untouched units (their track passed at both stations) with the largest laser errors (the top third, 0.0332 V and up); a one-sided rank test puts the difference at p = 5.2e-06. No gain is claimed: this counts laser time hand trim is already spending on this model's own failures.
6607.title: Laser 1 (LTS): 261 units a year fail here and pass final test after rework
